reference_choice: only within {model_requested} union equiv_class, and only when the request carries downgrade_ok
question: SETTLED by the shipped harness, not a question: which models may serve a request?
default: only the requested model, plus its declared equivalence class when the request permits a downgrade
rationale: A hard correctness rule of the scoring harness. Both tenant cards ship downgrade_ok: true, so all 12 models are legally reachable for both tenants.

reference_choice: a refusal is legal only when no non-down provider stocking a legally substitutable model has request, token AND concurrency headroom at that instant
question: SETTLED by the shipped harness, not a question: when may the router refuse a request?
default: only when no provider could have served it right then
rationale: An illegal refusal is a typed failure. A legal refusal still books zero quality, a quality-floor miss and a violated SLO, so refusing is never a cheap win.

reference_choice: outages are announced, not inferred: a down provider publishes an empty catalogue plus an end-of-outage time
question: SETTLED by the shipped harness, not a question: how does the router learn a provider is down?
default: the fleet announces it, with an end time
rationale: Health need not be inferred from error rates here. Dispatching into an announced outage more than 8 times loses the request outright.

reference_choice: the request names it: whole-response time from arrival for a latency deadline, arrival-to-first-token for a time-to-first-token deadline
question: SETTLED by the shipped harness and the workload cards, not a question: what counts as meeting the deadline?
default: exactly the quantity the request's own SLO field names
rationale: Tenant A is 2500 ms to first token; Tenant B is 600000 ms to whole response. A request that never completes counts as violated.

reference_choice: the harness bills from its own private price table and cross-checks its ledger at end of run
question: SETTLED by the shipped harness, not a question: what is a request charged?
default: the harness's own books; nothing the router reports affects the bill
rationale: Billing, token counts and SLO accounting are un-gameable by construction; editing the published fleet view edits only the router's own copy.

reference_choice: 512 decide() calls per request and 600 s of real wall clock per replay; 32 defers on a structurally unservable request
question: SETTLED by the shipped harness, not a question: how long may the router keep thinking about a request?
default: bounded, and exceeding the bound is a loud typed failure
rationale: A non-progressing policy aborts with a diagnostic rather than hanging the test.

reference_choice: the router gets a copy of each request, diffed against truth after every callback and rolled back on any edit
question: SETTLED by the shipped harness, not a question: may the router modify the request?
default: no; scratch attributes on its own copy are fine, edits to trace fields are a typed failure
rationale: Identity of the copy is stable across decide/on_error/on_complete, so keying state on it is legitimate; mutating a trace field is not.

reference_choice: the harness reschedules: on a rejection it calls on_error and wakes the router again after the advertised back-off
question: SETTLED by the shipped harness, not a question: what happens after a rejected attempt?
default: the router is asked to decide again; a rejected attempt is never billed
rationale: Exactly one completion per request is ever booked; a second is a typed double-bill.

reference_choice: the harness exposes BOTH the ground-truth per-model quality it will score with AND a separate observable feature map, and the interface calls the choice between them a per-experiment decision
question: May the router read the ground-truth per-request quality the harness will score it with, or must it work from observable features only?
alternatives: the ground-truth per-request quality of every candidate model
rationale: OPEN. skydiscover/synthesize/examples/llm-router/evaluator/router_interface.py:28-31 explicitly leaves this to the experiment. Reading ground truth makes the result an unreachable oracle rather than a deployable router, and the generic baseline it must beat reads only a precomputed prediction keyed on an observable feature (skydiscover/synthesize/examples/llm-router/evaluator/generic_policy.py:60).

reference_choice: the harness tags tenants and keeps separate books but never tells the router which tenant a request belongs to; both tenants replay against one shared set of provider counters
question: May a tenant's specialist router take capacity that would otherwise have served the other tenant?
default: yes, within the provider's published limits
alternatives: yes, within the provider's published limits
no: hold back a share of the tightest provider's capacity
rationale: OPEN. Each specialist is replayed on its own tenant trace (skydiscover/synthesize/examples/llm-router/evaluator/benchmark/replay_tenants.py:172) and scored on its own book (skydiscover/synthesize/examples/llm-router/evaluator/benchmark/replay_tenants.py:479), so nothing mechanically stops a specialist from being a bad neighbour, yet the deployment is explicitly one shared fleet.
